source_title: On debut, Jio 2nd most valuable company, behind only parent Reliance Industries
source_excerpt: MUMBAI: Jio Platforms, the telecoms-to-technology arm of the RIL group, had a blockbuster listing on Wednesday, becoming the second most valued company in India and the fifth most valued telecom services provider in the world, on debut.The stock listed at Rs 1,358, a 21% premium over its initial public offering price of Rs 1,119, and rallied to close the session at Rs 1,419, up 27%. This gave the company a market capitalisation of Rs 13.1 lakh crore, putting it behind only its parent Reliance Industries (Rs 15.7 lakh crore) but ahead of its peer Bharti Airtel (Rs 12.2 lakh crore), exchange data showed. Dhirubhai Ambani, her grandfather, had then said his objective to list was to take the company to the public and not just limit the gains from it to a handful of investors. Dhirubhai believed that anyone in India, however humble their beginnings were, deserved a share in the countryâs growth, as part-owners. âHe (had) asked ordinary families to trust him. And they did, with their savings, and with their dreams. Almost 50 years later, that trust has come full circle,â she said.Jio has about 54 crore customers. Its hugely successful IPO was subscribed over 22 times, with nearly 1.3 crore investors wanting to have a pie in the company. However, late buying, believed to be mainly by foreign funds, took the stock price beyond Rs 1,400 and the companyâs market cap beyond Rs 13 lakh crore, exchange data showed. The hugely successful IPO and the listing also took the RIL group to the top slot among the most valued business houses in India. At a combined market cap of Rs 30.3 lakh crore, it just raced past the incumbent Tata group, now at Rs 25.4 lakh crore, data from ETIntelligence showed.During the listing ceremony, Jio Platforms director Anant Ambani said he wanted to express gratitude to the millions who believed in Jio. He also paid rich tributes to his grandfather, Dhirubhai Ambani, and his father, Mukesh Ambani, âwho dreamt big and believed Bharat should not be behind anyoneâ.Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani said that in the next ten years, the companyâs aim is âto democratise every technology that can transform Indian lives: AI, cloud, connected devices, connectivity even from space, and digital services not yet imagined. After the first quote at Rs 1,358, the stock touched a high of Rs 1,424 and a low of Rs 1,357. On listing day, between the two bourses, about 19.4 crore Jio shares were traded.
